CanonicalStatus.description:
How the page's identity URL was chosen.

``self``          declared canonical equals the page's own URL
``declared``      a different, in-scope canonical was declared and is used
``missing``       none declared; the normalised final URL is used
``out_of_scope``  declared canonical is off-site; ignored, final URL used
``invalid``       declared canonical is unparseable; ignored, final URL used

Precedence at persistence (prevents identity flip-flop): a ``self`` or
``missing`` document is the AUTHORITY for its identity URL. A ``declared``
(alias) document may create identity X only while X has no version from an
authoritative document; once it has, the alias records ``known_urls`` Y -> X
plus a ``duplicate_canonical`` issue and writes no version. Within one run,
the authoritative document for X always wins over aliases of X.
CanonicalStatus.title: CanonicalStatus

ErrorCode.description:
Stable machine-readable error codes.

Codes are ``snake_case``. A client may branch on a code but must never
branch on ``message``, which is human-readable and may be reworded at any
time. Adding a member in a later phase is additive and non-breaking.

The ONLY error body any endpoint returns.

exceptions. ``request_id`` is how a caller correlates a failure with the
server logs instead.

message.description: Human-readable summary. Never branch on this.
message.title: Message

request_id.description: Correlates this failure with server logs.
request_id.title: Request Id

Distinct from :class:`~ken_contracts.health.ReadinessStatus`: a dependency
is *described* by this enum, whereas the service as a whole is *judged* by

LinkResolution.description:
Whether an internal link's destination is known (computed at read time).

``resolved``        the destination URL maps to a known, live page
``broken``          the destination returned 404/410, or maps to a page now gone
``unresolved``      not (yet) observed: beyond crawl limits, robots-blocked or errored
``not_applicable``  the link is not internal

Offset/limit rather than cursors: the Phase 5 review inbox needs jumpable
pages and stable total counts more than it needs consistency under

PublicationState.description:
Publication state as the source reports it.

The public web crawler can only observe ``published`` (a page served with
HTTP 200). Drafts are visible only through an export or a CMS read API.
``unknown`` is the honest default when a source does not say.
PublicationState.title: PublicationState

ReadinessResponse.description:
``GET /ready`` -- aggregate readiness.

HTTP status mapping, implemented in the router and asserted by tests:

==================  =====  ===============================
aggregate status    code   headers
==================  =====  ===============================
ready               200    Cache-Control: no-store
degraded            200    Cache-Control: no-store
not_ready           503    no-store, Retry-After: 5
==================  =====  ===============================

A probe that itself raises yields 503 with that check marked ERROR -- never
a 500, because an unhandled exception in a readiness probe is still a
readiness answer.
ReadinessResponse.title: ReadinessResponse

ReadinessStatus.description:
Aggregate verdict over all dependency checks.

The distinction between DEGRADED and NOT_READY is the whole point of the
``required`` flag on each check: an optional dependency that is missing
degrades the service without making it unready. In Phase 0 pgvector and
Ollama are both optional, so their absence must not take the API down.
ReadinessStatus.title: ReadinessStatus

RunCounters.description:
Run accounting. Invariant (checked by tests)::

pages_fetched == pages_created + pages_changed + pages_unchanged
                 + pages_duplicate + pages_failed
RunCounters.title: RunCounters

RunStatus.description:
Lifecycle of one ingestion run.

``failed`` means the run itself could not complete (the source could not
start, or an unexpected error aborted it). Per-URL problems never fail a
run: they are recorded as issues and give ``completed_with_errors``.
RunStatus.title: RunStatus
